best_for: Push 3 owners who need the firmware update file, the recovery image or the Windows USB audio driver, for example to repair a unit or update it from a computer.

points.title: Only useful with the hardware
points.text: This is the software side of Ableton's Push 3 controller: the firmware update package, the recovery image, the Windows USB audio drivers and the published GPL source. Without a Push it does nothing.

points.title: The hardware is the cost
points.text: Ableton lists Push 3 standalone at USD 1,799 and the computer-tethered Push 3 at USD 999, and both were on sale at the time of reading. An Upgrade Kit turns the tethered model into a standalone one later. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Live Intro comes with it
points.text: A Push purchase includes Live 12 Intro. Standard (USD 349) and Suite (USD 749) are separate, and some instruments and features need them, such as Stem Separation, which needs Live 12.3 Suite and Push software 2.3 or later.

points.title: Versions move with Live
points.text: Each Push release ships alongside the Live release with the matching number, for example Push 2.4.16 with Live 12.4.16 on October 30, 2026. That release had no Push-specific changes.

points.title: Updating without a computer
points.text: A standalone Push can fetch updates over Wi-Fi from its Software tab. Keep the power supply plugged in while it updates: since 2.4.3, Ableton warns that some units on USB-C power alone failed to reboot.

points.title: What the standalone model packs
points.text: Standalone units carry an Intel Core i3-1115G4, 8 GB of RAM, a 256 GB SSD and a battery rated for up to 2.5 hours, plus a built-in audio interface on both models.

points.title: Current release only
points.text: Windows and macOS each list only the current package, so older Push software versions need another source.
